text: With a fraction p of a program parallelizable, the best possible speedup on n processors is 1/((1-p) + p/n). This limit is known as ___ law.
explanation: At p = 0.95 — ninety-five percent parallel, which is very good — the ceiling is 20 no matter how many processors you buy, and on 24 cores you would get about 13. At p = 0.5 the ceiling is 2. The sequential part dominates, which is why Chapter 18's insistence on measuring first applies with particular force here: concurrency also costs correctness, and paying that for a 1.3-times speedup is a bad trade.
